lines: You break your wrist, and the hospital bill is 8,000 dollars. Because you have health insurance for 120 dollars a month, you pay 2,800 and the insurer pays 5,200.
Insurance works by pooling risk. Thousands of people each pay a little, and most stay healthy, so their money covers the few who need it. What you pay to stay covered is the premium.
When you get care, you first pay the deductible. After that you pay your share, the coinsurance, like 20 percent. And once you hit the out-of-pocket maximum, the insurer pays everything.
On the 8,000 dollar wrist: 1,500 deductible, plus 20 percent of the other 6,500, which is 1,300. You pay 2,800.
To choose a health plan, add a year of premiums to what you'd pay for care. A low premium plan wins in healthy years. A high premium plan can win in a big year.
Car insurance: liability pays for damage you cause to others, and almost every state requires it. Collision fixes your car after a crash. Comprehensive covers theft, hail and deer.
If you rent, the landlord's insurance doesn't cover your things. Renters insurance does, often for about 15 to 20 dollars a month.
Pick deductibles your emergency fund can pay. Insurance covers the disasters; your fund covers the deductibles.
Emperor penguins huddle through the Antarctic winter, each taking a turn on the cold edge. Your premium is your turn on the edge, so the group can carry you when the storm hits.
